newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich committed to improving D.C. - spokeswoman.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich committed to improving D.C. - spokeswoman.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich is committed to improving the District of Columbia but had no immediate comment on President Clinton's plan because he had not seen details, a spokeswoman for the speaker said Tuesday.
"We have not seen the contents of it," Lauren Maddox, a spokeswoman for the Republican from Georgia, said.
"Of course his (Gingrich's) concern is that there not just be some kind of a transfer of money or additional government money, that in fact there be significant structural reforms," she said.

The White House announced a $3.9 billion five-year federal aid plan for Washington, D.C., and said it was ending the $3.56 billion federal payment to the city that would have been made over that period.

Gingrich was also concerned about whether there would be some tax incentives included in Clinton's proposal that would give people incentive to move back into Washington and for businesses in the district to create more jobs, Maddox said.
"He (Gingrich) looks forward to seeing what the president has on the table, and looks forward to being briefed on the substance of it and whether those two things are addressed," she said.
